title: The rational transition shift is uniquely fixed by localizing the normalized integral shift.
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, finite intermediate coefficient fields $E\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], and an arbitrary scheme $Y$. No finite-type, separatedness, or invertibility assumption on $Y$ is imposed. Write $\mathcal I_F=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_F)$ for the intrinsic integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $\mathcal R_F=\mathcal I_F[1/\varpi_F]$ and $Q_F:\mathcal I_F\to\mathcal R_F$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Use the fixed induced integer shifts on these categories [def-weil-triangulated-category, lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated], whose degree-one functor is scalar extension of the integral shift and whose degree-one comparison for $Q_F$ is the identity [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Let $T:\mathcal I_E\to\mathcal I_L$ be the restricted completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible], with the fixed ordinary-to-completed normalized coherent integer-shift structure of [lem-route-integral-transition-comm-shift-exists-unique]; denote its components by $t_{n,K}:T(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(TK)[n]$. Let $F:\mathcal R_E\to\mathcal R_L$ be the specified rational scalar transition of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], so that $F(Q_EK)=Q_L(TK)$ and $F(f\otimes a)=T(f)\otimes\iota(a)$ for the inclusion $\iota:E\hookrightarrow L$.

There exists exactly one coherent integer-shift structure $c$ on this fixed functor $F$ whose degree-one hom component satisfies
$$
 c_{1,Q_EK}=Q_L(t_{1,K})\qquad(K\in\mathcal I_E).
$$
The equality is after the displayed object identifications and the fixed degree-one shift identifications (equivalently, it is the heterogeneous equality in the recorded Lean signature). Here a coherent integer-shift structure means natural isomorphisms $c_n:F(-[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(F-)[n]$ for all $n\in\mathbf Z$, with the canonical degree-zero comparison and the shift-addition equation. Explicitly, if $A^{\mathcal R}_{n,m}:[n+m]\xrightarrow{\sim}[n][m]$ denotes the fixed shift-addition isomorphism, the equation at $X$ is
$$
 c_{n+m,X}=F(A^{\mathcal R_E}_{n,m,X})\,;\,c_{m,X[n]}\,;\,[m](c_{n,X})\,;\,(A^{\mathcal R_L}_{n,m,FX})^{-1},
$$
where semicolons denote composition in the order written. Uniqueness is equality of the entire coherent structure, not only of the degree-one components. Every rational object is literally $Q_EK$; no idempotent completion is used.

theorem transitionCommShift_existsUnique (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) :
    ∃! c : (transition D l hl Ω Y E L h).CommShift ℤ,
      (fun [commInst : (transition D l hl Ω Y E L h).CommShift ℤ] ↦
        ∀ K : Stage D l hl Ω Y E,
          HEq (((transition D l hl Ω Y E L h).commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app K)
            ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) Y).map
              (((sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension D.p l hl
                (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L)
                (coefficientInclusion l Ω E L h) Y).commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app K.obj)))
        (commInst := c) := by
  sorry
